key_insight: Ghost tasking adds auxiliary output tasks so parametrized Gaussian Processes can handle linear differential systems that are otherwise non-controllable, while keeping the model compact.
engineering_relevance: This enables physics-informed GP models for inverse problems and low-data settings without requiring many outputs or a strictly parametrizable system.
method: Introduce auxiliary "ghost" tasks to make a system effectively parametrizable.
Use the resulting parametrization to construct parametrized Gaussian Processes algorithmically.
Provide computer-algebra syntax for polynomial and rational systems, with theory extended to meromorphic coefficients.
evidence_signal: The paper reports three experiments and systematic comparisons against the only other method applicable across all cases, with especially strong performance in an inverse-problem setting under very limited data.
watch_item: Practical use depends on constructing valid ghost tasks and symbolic parametrizations, which may be nontrivial for complex systems or software workflows.
paper_title: Ghost tasking for parametrized Gaussian Processes solving linear differential equations
